title: Emit blocked Outcome for governed synchronization conflicts
outOfScope: Manual creation, editing, or deletion of any blocked Outcome, start receipt, archive evidence, or rebase state.
Manual conflict resolution, force-push, merge, release, tag, provider branch deletion, or GitHub required-check changes.
Changing the success path of ai-synchronize-work-item or weakening ai-transition-conflict-successor validation.

riskAssessment.reason: A missing or malformed conflict Outcome can strand a legitimate Work Item; an over-broad writer could falsely authorize a successor or corrupt the normal synchronization path.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: RayIori approved design A and standing automatic execution; implementation remains limited to #709's real synchronization-conflict Outcome gap.

preReviewWarnings: Review the conflict-only guard, exact target-root ownership, and preservation of the source checkpoint/abort behavior.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: When an authorized ai-synchronize-work-item checkpoint encounters a rebase conflict, it automatically aborts the rebase and persists a validated red blocked Outcome with failedGate synchronization_conflict before returning failure.

The derived Human Benefit Report and generated cockpit status expose the same blocked Outcome; the writer resolves every path inside the explicit target worktree, preserves the original checkpoint commit and source Contract/Start Receipt, and records the blocked state through a distinct authorized recovery-evidence commit after the abort.
The normal clean synchronization path and all conflict-successor validation remain fail-closed; a successor is accepted only after the real source conflict Outcome exists.
A regression invokes the production synchronization path rather than handwriting Outcome JSON, proves the red Outcome/report, then proves the conflict-successor receipt can bind it.
Lifecycle documentation and generated capability projections describe the automatic conflict Outcome and its recovery boundary.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Outcome evidence is generated by canonical code, never handwritten to satisfy a transition guard.

intent.problem: A real governed synchronization conflict currently checkpoints and aborts safely but emits no blocked Outcome, while the merged conflict-successor route requires exactly that Outcome. This leaves an active Work Item unable to enter its documented current-main successor route.
constraints: Use the existing #709 corrective Issue and do not create another Issue for this production-path omission.
Persist the Outcome only after the synchronization command proves a conflict and has automatically aborted the rebase.
Use the existing validated Outcome/Human Report pipeline, made explicit-target-root safe where necessary; do not handwrite lifecycle evidence.

Preserve the original checkpoint commit, source Contract, start receipt, normal synchronization behavior, and conflict-successor validation; the Summary may be updated only with canonical blocked Outcome state and committed as recovery evidence.
The user approved automatic execution and evidence-bound supersession/quarantine; this Work Item does not authorize any release or provider cleanup.
intent.rationale: A single canonical blocked-Outcome pipeline makes the failure visible through the required red traffic-light surface and supplies the immutable evidence that the existing successor command already validates.
